turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall endeavor to do so, ma’am. Though I fear I might stumble over the threshold, it’s… it’s a rather imposing door, isn’t it?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Indeed, a rather imposing door, is it not? It has witnessed so much… so much hope, dashed against its panels, like a fragile butterfly against a storm. I want to see her, Pip. Bring Estella to me, dear boy.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, yes, ma'am, certainly. I… I shall try my very best to find Estella, though the house is rather… extensive, isn’t it? I do hope I won't get lost, and… and disappoint you, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Lost, you fear? Lost, dear boy, is a state of mind, is it not? But do not fret about the house; fret about what lies within its walls - the memories, the echoes... Bring Estella, Pip. Bring her to me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall attempt to locate Miss Estella with the utmost diligence, ma’am. It’s just… these corridors seem to twist and turn, and the shadows… they are rather… pervasive, aren’t they? I wouldn't wish to wander aimlessly and cause you further distress, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Distress? Oh, distress is my constant companion, Pip. It clings to me like the dust that settles upon these forgotten things, and I welcome it, in a fashion. But bring Estella, dear boy; she is a bright spark in this… this perpetual twilight.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I shall endeavour to do precisely that, Miss Havisham. Though, if I may be so bold as to inquire, is Miss Estella… is she often found within the corridors? I wouldn't want to disturb her, you see, if she were engaged in… in something of importance.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Engaged, you say? My dear boy, Estella is ever engaged, in one pursuit or another. It is a quality I… I fostered, you understand. Find her, Pip; find her, and bring her to me, to witness the… the stillness.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, Miss Havisham. I… I shall certainly try my very best to find Miss Estella, and to bring her to you as you request. Though… though I confess, I do find myself feeling rather… rather lost in this labyrinthine house, and I wouldn't wish to delay her arrival unduly, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Lost, are you, my dear? A fitting sentiment, wouldn't you agree? For I, too, am lost, lost within the chambers of a memory that refuses to… to release its hold. Find Estella, Pip; she understands the art of being lost, in her own peculiar way.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, yes, Miss Havisham. I... I shall attempt to locate Miss Estella with the utmost diligence, though I do hope she isn't occupied with… with matters of great consequence, you see. It would be most distressing to interrupt her, and I wouldn’t want to incur your displeasure, ma’am.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Distressing, you say? My dear boy, distressing is the very air I breathe! It clings to the tapestries, it settles upon the dust… it is the perfume of my existence. Find Estella, Pip; find her, and let her tell you of true distress.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: If she permits it, Miss Havisham, I might, perhaps, venture to enquire as to the… the direction in which Miss Estella might be residing? It would, I believe, be most imprudent of me to wander aimlessly, lest I inadvertently cause some… some disruption to your, ah, atmosphere.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Imprudent, you say? My dear Pip, imprudence is the very lifeblood of a shattered heart! To wander aimlessly… yes, perhaps that is precisely what you *should* do. It mirrors my own wandering, you see; a perpetual circling of the wreckage.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Indeed, Miss Havisham. I… I shall endeavor to wander, as you suggest, though I confess a certain apprehension regarding the… the potential for encountering objects of… of fragility, you understand. It would be most unfortunate should I accidentally dislodge something, and cause further… further disturbance.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Fragility, my dear boy? Everything is fragile, everything… especially hope. It shatters, you see, like the finest porcelain dropped upon a stone floor—a sound I remember… oh, a sound I remember all too well. Go on, Pip, wander. Let your footsteps echo in the silence, a mournful accompaniment to my… my perpetual stillness.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Oh, yes, Miss Havisham. I… I shall endeavor to do so, though I feel a certain… responsibility, you see, to be… careful. I wouldn't wish to, in any way, amplify the… the stillness, or… or disturb anything further.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Careful, you say? A commendable trait, my dear Pip, but caution is a poor substitute for courage. Courage to face the dust, the decay, the… the emptiness. Go on, then, wander amongst it, and tell me, Pip, what do *you* see?

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I… I see dust, Miss Havisham. Everywhere, a great deal of dust, and… and shadows, of course. It seems… it seems as though time itself has settled upon everything, like a… a heavy cloth, you see.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: A heavy cloth, you say? Yes, a cloth… a shroud, almost. It smothers the light, doesn't it, Pip? And what lies *beneath* the cloth, my dear boy? What secrets does it conceal?

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: You can do that. Call Estella. At the door.
